pr_title: native port: Mirror the zephyr thread name onto native threads
pr_body:
When debugging native applications it is useful to know which thread is being debugged. Currently, all thread names are being displayed as "zephyr", making this hard.
The changes in this PR changes this to display the zephyr thread names, given that `CONFIG_THREAD_NAME` is enabled.

To avoid adding posix-specific code in the kernel, this is handled by adding a new optional arch API to the kernel interface.

Fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/52223.

issue_context.title: native port: Mirror the zephyr thread name onto native threads
issue_context.body:
The idea is to have the thread name mirrored from the zephyr task struct into the native OS thread name. It would make debugging easier, since there is no second guessing which thread is which.

From my research the only portable/posix way to set the thread name `prctl(PR_SET_NAME, "...")`, which can only set the thread name of the currently executing thread. In posix-zephyr-land, this only enables setting the name once at the start. The other way is to rely on the `pthread_setname_np` which is not the same on all posix-capable platforms, but allows to set the name of any thread and therefore would allow `k_thread_name_set` to work.

Maybe somebody has a fix for this problem and a solution that would allow zephyr to implement this feature.

It's possible that you're confusing `CONFIG_ARCH_POSIX` and `CONFIG_POSIX_API`.

Note, they are mutually exclusive at the moment (you cannot use Zephyr's POSIX subsystem currently when building for `native_posix`).

It is unlikely that this will ever be fixed for the POSIX arch.
